correctness.rationale: The fixed-support uncensored preprint defines the stated symmetric kernel and two-sided cutoff. Independently, writing G(x)=F(x)−x reduces the contrast to the integral over [0,1] of 2(1−2x)G−G². With t=2x−1 the L2 and L4 contributions to G are (t³−t)/4 and (7t⁵−10t³+3t)/16; integrating gives (462b+11ab−33b²−5a²)/6930. On |a|≤1 the upper root makes the density negative at the midpoint, whereas the lower root satisfies 0≤b<1/80 and b>0 away from a=0. In u=x(1−x) the density is concave for a≤0, with both endpoints strictly positive (including a=−1); for a≥0 use L4≥−3/7 and L2≥−1/2. Orthogonality gives normalization and excludes uniformity at a≠0. The first conditional projection has derivative F(x)+x−1, so with positive density it is not constant; the bounded-kernel CLT has variance 4 Var(Q_F(X)), where Q_F is the primitive of that derivative. The null gives 1/45. Independent polynomial integration at a=−1 agrees with the variance polynomial in the source; bounding its positive b terms at 1/80 and dropping its negative ones gives a strict upper bound below 1/45. The centered Gaussian limit then yields 0.01718802635… at 5%, and a limit strictly between zero and one for every asserted alternative. The frozen checker was inspected, not run. The inference does not extend to censored data or support estimation.

value.rationale: This is an operationally meaningful failure case for a specified published test. Even restricting to an everywhere-positive symmetric density, thereby ruling out skewness as the explanation, exact nonuniform zero-contrast alternatives persist. The higher Legendre mode has zero first-order contrast by orthogonality and the lower mode compensates its quadratic contribution; this gives a principled slice, not an arbitrary two-parameter example. Complete admissibility on the supplied interval and an explicit 1.72% limit at 5% nominal add information beyond the nearby nominal and mildly subnominal examples. No finite-sample performance or general classification outside that slice is claimed.
